title: Affine-section dictionary for the resolution flat base-change map
statement: Let f:X→S be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, let g:S′→S and g′=pullback.snd g f be flat, and let F be quasi-coherent on X. Take injective resolutions I of F and J of g′*F and an augmentation-preserving lift t:I→g′_*J as in [def-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-resolution-construction]. Fix p≥0 and affine opens V⊆S, W⊆S′ with W⊆g⁻¹V. Put A=Γ(S,V), B=Γ(S′,W), with A-algebra structure on B from g.appLE V W, U=f⁻¹V, h=(f.resLE V U) followed by V.toSpecΓ:U→Spec A, and N=F pulled back along U.ι [def-pc-module-pullback]. Then the actual map on sections Γ(W,flatBaseChangeResolutionBeta f g I J t p) is bijective if and only if H.baseChange for h,N,B,p [def-pc-flat-cohomology-comparison] is bijective. The assertion identifies these local maps, without asserting that either is invertible.

source.place: Lemma 30.5.2, first paragraph of the proof (reduction of (1) to (2)); comparison from Tag 02N7; affine sections by 01XJ and 01XK; module/abelian agreement by 03FD.

proof.text: Choose restricted resolution data D using flatBaseChangeMap_sections_choices. Apply the normalized affine dictionary to D to obtain e_H and the bijective B-linear maps a and b, with their two normalization formulas.

For a pure tensor s tensor xi, apply the source normalization and B-linearity of the section map of beta. The section formula for the augmentation-preserving lift t identifies beta on the unit of sourceClass(e_H inverse xi) with targetClass of the cohomological pullback. Naturality of beta with restriction to W and the target normalization give beta_W(a(s tensor xi))=b(H.baseChange(s tensor xi)).

Tensor induction proves the same equality for all tensors: zero and addition follow from additivity. Therefore beta_W composed with a equals b composed with H.baseChange. Since a and b are bijective, composition with them preserves and reflects bijectivity, giving the stated iff.
